title: The Cute kitten in the basket
subtitle: 动物世界 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 动物世界（人与自然·自然生态·动物世界）
meta: 主题语境：动物世界（人与自然·自然生态·动物世界）　|　核心词汇：cute　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 cute 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1951 the planner wrote of ① a cute kitten in the basket in the report, and everybody in the district said at once that it was ② cuter than the one named there the year before. Three years on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the planner, who never explained anything, had done it at once and gone home; it was the cute ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the cutest kitten in the basket anybody in the district had ever seen, or so the report for March 1945 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too cute to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the citizen who had come to help; the cute ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the plan at the far square, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a cute trick with the cards, and said that no citizen in his right mind would call it ⑥ as cute as the trick with the cards they had once had in the old district. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was cute or not, and he said so.

By 1958 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the report. What the line asked for was ⑦ something cute, and nothing besides. The citizen from the next district called the whole plan ⑧ quite cute; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the report kept the names of the cute ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1961, in the rain, she wrote of another cute kitten in the basket in the same report, and the work, which took two years, seemed ⑨ cuter than anybody had expected. ⑩ The cutest trick with the cards in the whole district, she said in 1963, was the one she could never quite name; the cute ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 可爱（前置定语 a cute kitten in the basket：1951 年规划员在规划报告里记下的那件可爱的猫崽）
B. adj. 可爱／精巧（比较级 cuter than：文中两处，一处比篮里的猫崽，一处比预想）
C. adj. 可爱／精巧（最高级 the cutest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 可爱（表语 too cute to do：母亲觉得它太可爱，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 精巧（前置定语 a cute trick with the cards：叔叔把整件事称作一桩精巧的小把戏）
F. adj. 精巧（同级比较 as cute as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩纸牌的小把戏相比）
G. adj. 精巧（后置定语 something cute：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 精巧（受程度副词修饰 quite cute：那位市民的评价）

items.q: a cute kitten in the basket
the cutest kitten in the basket anybody
a cute trick with the cards
The cutest trick with the cards in

answers.why: cute 意为“可爱”，1951 年规划员在规划报告里记下的是“一件可爱的猫崽”，此处作前置定语 a cute kitten in the basket。
cute 意为“可爱”，此处用比较级 cuter than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
cute 意为“可爱”，规划报告上 三月 那行字说它是街区里最可爱的一件，故用最高级 the cutest kitten in the basket。
cute 意为“可爱”，母亲认为这件东西“太可爱了，谁也用不上”，too cute to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
cute 意为“精巧”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩精巧的小把戏”，此处作前置定语 a cute trick with the cards。
cute 意为“精巧”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩纸牌的小把戏一样精巧”，同级比较用 as cute as。
cute 意为“精巧”，规划报告上那半行字要的是“精巧的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something cute。
cute 意为“精巧”，邻街区来的那位市民认为这套计划“相当精巧”，quite 修饰原级 cute。
cute 意为“精巧”，1961 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要精巧”，故用比较级 cuter than。
cute 意为“精巧”，母亲 1963 年说的是“整个街区里最精巧的那一桩”，故用最高级 the cutest trick with the cards。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1951 年，规划员在规划报告里记下了一件可爱的猫崽。（a cute kitten in the basket）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更可爱。（cuter than …）
母亲觉得它太可爱，谁也用不上。（too cute to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩精巧的小把戏。（a cute trick with the cards）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩纸牌的小把戏一样精巧。（as cute as …）
到了 1958 年，规划报告上只剩半行字：要的是一件精巧的东西。（something cute）
answers: In 1951 the planner wrote of a cute kitten in the basket in the report.
Everybody said it was cuter than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too cute to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a cute trick with the cards.
He said nobody would call it as cute as the trick with the cards they had once had.
By 1958 the report asked for nothing but something cute.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 cute 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1951 the planner wrote of a cute kitten in the basket in the report, and nobody forgot it.
It was the cutest kitten in the basket in the district, or so the report says.
My mother thought it too cute to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a cute trick with the cards, and nobody argued with him.
The citizen from the next district called the plan quite cute, and everybody laughed.
The cute ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
